strengths: Novel application of e-value framework to equilibrium monitoring, first anytime-valid approach to sequential testing in multi-agent games
Sound mathematical framework with rigorous guarantees (FWER and FDR control, tight detection time bounds)
Improved information requirements compared to prior work (Babichenko et al. 2017): does not require knowledge of equilibrium strategy in normal-form setting
Comprehensive treatment including extensions to correlated/coarse-correlated equilibria, stochastic games, and alternative testing frameworks with detailed proofs
Well-designed FDR control via e-BH procedure with proven speedup over FWER (Proposition 2.9, empirically validated with 1.15× in 2×2 game)
Strong experimental validation of theoretical predictions: O(1/ε²) scaling law (Figure 2) and robustness to unknown deviations (Figure 3)
Reproducibility: code made publicly available with detailed experimental documentation
weaknesses: I.i.d. assumption on joint action profiles is highly restrictive, excluding learning dynamics, correlated strategies, and temporal dependencies common in practice
Requires pre-specification of slack parameter η > 0 (minimum detectable deviation) with no principled guidance for practitioners; this is a practical barrier to adoption

Limited experimental scope: only synthetic games (2×2, 20-player Rock-Paper-Scissors, gridworlds); no real-world validation or comparison to alternative methods (change-point detection, classical corrections)
Gap between Sections 2 and 3: different testing frameworks (regret-based vs likelihood-ratio) weaken the 'unified' contribution claim
Support condition requirement (π_i(a|s) > 0 when π^(1)_i(a|s) > 0) in stochastic games is addressed only via ad-hoc smoothing; adds hyperparameter tuning burden
Practical guidance is missing: no principled methods for selecting α, b, η or analyzing computational complexity; detection times in thousands of rounds
Theoretical optimality of λ* = η does not translate to practice (Section H.1.4 shows larger λ can empirically outperform); discrepancy inadequately discussed
Dense presentation with key material relegated to appendices; intuition for why regret-like increments capture equilibrium violations could be clearer
